lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Early moment where Elizabeth says she already understood him, establishing their private shorthand.

lines.text: If I did not love you, how I would begin now!
lines.note: Robert declares that love for Elizabeth would make him begin loving now, a vivid early turning point.

lines.text: And something I said in my letter, which was wrong to say and I am sorry to think of—forgive me that, ever beloved—but you have forgiven, I know.
lines.note: Elizabeth admits she said something wrong and asks Robert to forgive her, matching the sorry occasion.

lines.text: Will you come, dearest, after all?
lines.note: Elizabeth asks whether Robert will come after all, capturing the anxious middle of their separation.

lines.text: I will say no more, praying you to forgive whatever you shall judge to need forgiveness here,—dearest Ba!
lines.note: Robert prays that Elizabeth forgive whatever needs forgiveness, a direct apology in the correspondence.

lines.text: Will you not forgive me a word so spoken, Robert? will you rather set it against me as if habitually I threw to you levities in change for earnest devotion?—you imply that of me.
lines.note: Elizabeth asks Robert to forgive a lightly spoken word, continuing their apology-and-forgiveness thread.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: Elizabeth writes that she has lost Flush, a sharp emotional turn that only they would recognise.

lines.text: Will you be tolerant, my Ba, and forgive me—till to-morrow at least—when, what with physic, what with impatience, I shall be better one way or another?
lines.note: Robert asks Elizabeth to be tolerant and forgive him until he is better, another direct apology.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Elizabeth reports that Flush is found and lying on the sofa, resolving the earlier loss.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Elizabeth writes after the secret wedding day, saying she is not slain outright by it.

lines.text: Thank you a thousand times for the note, my own Ba.
lines.note: Robert thanks Elizabeth a thousand times for her note and acknowledges the pain she bore for his sake.

lines.text: First, God is to be thanked for this great joy of hearing that you are better, my ever dearest—it is a joy that floats over all the other emotions.
lines.note: Elizabeth thanks God for hearing that Robert is better, ending on joy after the anxious weeks.
